noah: Hey team — just opened my first PR from branch noah/fastload-opt -> main. CI is failing lint checks and I'm not totally sure which style rules we enforce here. Also, who should I ping to review infra/runtime changes?

Talia: welcome onboard! :tada: Our contributor guide is at /docs/contributing/code-style.md. TL;DR: commit format is <type>(<scope>): short description (e.g., feat(runtime): optimize kv cache). Branch names: <user>/<short-desc> or include JIRA if you have one (e.g., NOAH-12/fastload). PR template requires the checklist filled out.

Mika: For runtime infra, ping @jared or @infra-team. If it's purely a config tweak small enough, 1 reviewer is okay; for behavior changes we prefer 2 reviewers including an SRE. Also make sure you add a unit test or a short integration snippet when modifying logic.

noah: thanks — the lint output shows ruff/black complaints. Here's the failing snippet:```
./runtime/fastload.py:42: F401 'typing.List' imported but unused
./runtime/fastload.py:118: E203 whitespace before ':' (black/ruff conflict?)
```

ci-bot: Lint step failed on commit 6f3a2b. Suggest running `pre-commit run --all-files` locally. See CI log: https://ci.redwood.internal/1932456789/1

Sri: If you haven't, run `pipx run ruff check .` or `pre-commit install && pre-commit run --all-files`. Our repo also has `make format` that runs black/isort/ruff with our config. Quick fixes: remove unused imports, don't reformat black-excluded slices manually.

Talia: One gotcha — we have a repo-level `.ruff.toml` that disables some rules; use the repo config. If you want, paste the small diff and I can point which changes are safe. For commit messages, we prefer conventional-ish format but don't enforce with a bot right now.

noah: ran `pre-commit` and fixed the imports. Pushed a force update. CI now shows lint passed but unit tests timed out in the integration suite. Any tips for flaky tests?

Mika: Flaky infra tests usually time out on CI decker stage. Re-run the job first. If it consistently times out, add `@flaky` marker on the test or increase the timeout per the test helper: `tests/integration/conftest.py` documents the knob. Also avoid making infra changes that touch cluster setup in the same PR as logic changes — keeps blamelist small.

noah: re-ran the job and it passed. Who should I add as reviewer? I modified runtime/fastload.py and a small test.

Jared: I'll take a look — adding myself as reviewer now. Quick reminder: please squash/fixup WIP commits before merge and fill the PR checklist (security/privacy review if you touched config). :eyes:

noah: awesome, thanks everyone. If anything else pops up, @talia I'll ping you for the checklist bits. :slightly_smiling_face:
